transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what finally brought me in is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I used to always make time for things—painting, hiking, my choir, even just Sunday family gatherings. And now... I don't know, even when I have a free hour, I just sit there. I'm just completely unable to care about any of it.
Do you still enjoy the activities you used to, or has the pleasure gone away?

Yeah, like I was just saying, the pleasure is really just gone. Um, I don't get any joy out of those things anymore. Even if I think about my painting or going to choir, I just... I don't care. The enjoyment just isn't there at all.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, it's been building for a while now. I'd say about eight months. It started right around the time I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at school.
Do you often feel sad or empty?

Yes, I do. Um, most days it just feels like there's this heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing right in the middle of a classroom full of students, or just sitting at home with my husband, and I still feel completely hollow. I just... I feel close to tears a lot of the time.
Do you still enjoy spending time with your husband and family, or has that changed too?

Yeah, that's changed too. Honestly, that's what finally brought me in to see you, because I just don't feel like myself anymore. I used to always make time for our Sunday family gatherings, along with hiking and the painting and choir I mentioned earlier. But now, even when I have a free hour to spend with them, I just sit there. I'm just... unable to care about any of it.
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Yes, I do. Um... especially with work. When anything goes wrong with the curriculum project, even just something really small, I keep thinking that I'm completely letting the students down. And then I start feeling like I'm wasting all the sacrifices my parents made for me to even have this kind of opportunity in the first place. It's just this constant guilt over every little mistake.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to, or feeling restless and fidgety?

No, not really. Um, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't think I'm talking or moving any slower than usual, and I'm not pacing around or feeling fidgety. Physically, my movements seem about the same as they always have.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?
No, I don't think so. Um, my clothes all still fit exactly the same as they usually do. I haven't really been stepping on a scale or anything, but my weight seems to be pretty stable.
Have you had any thoughts about death or wanting to die?

Yes, I have. Um... sometimes on late nights in the studio, I catch myself thinking that it would just be a relief if I didn't wake up. I haven't made an actual plan or anything like that, but... those thoughts really scare me. They scared me enough that I finally told my husband about them, because I realized I just couldn't keep handling them alone.
Have you experienced a significant loss of interest in most activities for at least two weeks?

Yes, definitely. Actually, that's what finally brought me in to see someone. I just... I don't feel like myself anymore. I used to always make time for things, you know? Painting, going hiking, singing in my choir, and our Sunday family gatherings. But lately, even when I have a free hour, I just sit there. I find myself completely unable to care about any of it.
Have you experienced any psychomotor agitation or retardation, such as feeling like you're moving slower than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or anything, and I'm not, you know, pacing around or feeling restless either. My energy is definitely low, but physically, my movements seem pretty normal.
Have you experienced a loss of interest in activities for more than two weeks, but less than two years?
Yes, it fits in that timeframe. I'd say this has been building for about eight months now. It really started right around the time I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at the school.
Have you experienced significant weight loss or gain since you started feeling this way?
No, not really. My weight has stayed pretty much the same. I haven't noticed any big changes, up or down, since all this started. My clothes still fit the same as they usually do.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel anxious. I mean, I don't find myself worrying about things any more than I normally would. It's not really a nervous feeling, so... no, anxiety hasn't really been an issue for me.
Have you experienced a depressive episode that has lasted for more than two years?

No, definitely not two years. Um, like I mentioned a minute ago, it's really just been about eight months or so. Before that started... no, I was doing fine. So it hasn't been anywhere near two years.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Not really, no. Honestly, that's what finally brought me in to see you today. I just don't feel like myself anymore. I used to make a point to find time for painting, hiking, my choir group, and our Sunday family gatherings. But now... even when I have a free hour, I just sit there. I'm just unable to care about any of it.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness and emptiness are present most of the day?

Yes, pretty much all day. It's... well, most days I just feel like there's this heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing right in the middle of a classroom full of students, or just at home with my husband, and I still feel completely hollow. Just... close to tears, honestly, no matter what I'm doing.
Would you say your depression is mild, moderate, or severe?

I'm not really sure how to rate it, honestly. I don't know what counts as mild or severe. I just know it's... it's really affecting my life, but I'm still getting out of bed and going to work, so maybe somewhere in the middle?
